## Design

### 2026-11-04: I basically started working on the project by reading the guide very carefully first before doing anything and acually understanding stuff and taking in account even small stuff. so first i started of

**3.6h**

I basically started working on the project by reading the guide very carefully first before doing anything and acually understanding stuff and taking in account even small stuff. so first i started off by placing the rp2040 symbol then wired the 1.1v and 3.3v to it's pins on the mcu, then after that i placed down all the required decoupling capacitors specifically for 1.1v : 8  0.1uF capacitors  and 1 1uF capacitor so a total of 9 capacitors and for the 3.3v 2 0.1 uF capacitors and 1 1uF capacitor. After doing all that i moved on to the USB c where i had a little of a problem because in the guide the usb that was used had 2 pairs of d+ and d- (data lines) but the symbol i placed had only 1 d+ and 1 d- so i took my time to look thru each usb c symbol to make sure i didn't make any errors and sure enough i found out i was using the wrong symbol but after that i wired gnd, the data pins (wich i also later connected to the mcu)  and lastly the vbus (wich is the power that will go to the mcu) had to go thru an LDO so following the guide i placed it down and connected all itìs required pins. And to finish off this entry i placed the crystal oscilators global labels so "XIN" and "XOUT".

### 2026-11-05: So after the last entry today i reopened the project and started working on everything else on the schematic and i was determined to finish but of course first of all i read the guide very carefully o

**5.3h**

So after the last entry today i reopened the project and started working on everything else on the schematic and i was determined to finish but of course first of all i read the guide very carefully once again and started working on the crystal oscillator and since last time i already placed the global nets for it, this time i had to wire it but when i placed the same exact symbol it only had 3 pins while the  guide had one with 4 and even tho they had the same name they had different pins in the guide pin 4 and 2 went to gnd but mine didnt have pin 4 so after a little playing aroud i found out in the symbol editor that since they both go to the same gnd pin kicad overlaps them and hides pin 4 so yeah that cool but at the same time i was freaking out because i couldn't find pin 4.  After finishing the wiring for the crystal i went ahead and started working on the flash memory where because the rp2040 doesn't have a built in one i had to place one and wire it to the mcu wich was the master to this W25Q128JVS wich is the slave in this case wich wasn't that hard to wire after all jsut understanding how the comunication worked beetween these took a while, now moving on to the last thing i did and the most painfull one was the headers where i had to place more than 30  global nets on the mcu but also copy them over to 2 generic 01x20 connectors and 1 generic 01x03 connector wich took a while also because in the guide we had to discard some pins and add others so you had to modify the structure. Now finally after i finished all of this i organized all the symbols neatly into boxes each with text showing what is inside and laslty i ran erc and found some errors where i had a couple of nets laying around not connected to anything (copies i forgot to delete) but also a gnd connection that looked connected but really wasn't after that all i had was 3 "Power pin not driven by any Output Power pins" errors wich the guide said not to consider. Next entry imma smart making the pcb.

### 2026-11-08: Well this is the part i hated the most (i will hate routing even more) where i had to place all the capacitors around wich took me a while simply because the capacitors that had to go to 3.3v where al

**1.4h**

Well this is the part i hated the most (i will hate routing even more) where i had to place all the capacitors around wich took me a while simply because the capacitors that had to go to 3.3v where all showing a net name and not directly gnd or 3.3v wich made it harder to know wich capacitor is wich and also wich capacitor goes to 3.3 v and 1.1v so it got very confusing to the point that i had to restart the whole layout but before i did that i went to the schematic and made some importanto changes: i left the capacitors connected in parallel but connected each individual one to 3.3 v and GND separatly so in the pcb editor it shows GND and 3.3V instead of "Label6.... " also forgot to mention i placed down resistors too
